FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A16
Safe eyes ride twelve seconds ahead, one block in town or four on highways, while the separate four second sight rule caps speed against visible distance. [A16]
Why it matters: group_hint look-vs-speed; prereq_hint sec04-F04; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F04, sec04-F25.
Source: [A16 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]
FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A17
Left turns bow to every oncoming vehicle and bike with double rechecks, whereas right turns on red need only a full stop, clear lefts and paths, and no banning sign. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint turn-yields; prereq_hint sec04-F06; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F06, sec04-F07.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A17
A dead signal legally becomes a stop sign for all, yet even a live fresh green still demands left right scans for red runners. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint signal-trust; prereq_hint sec04-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F06, sec04-F07.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A17
Heavy traffic forbids entering without far side room to dodge gridlock, but a blind corner invites a slow edge forward so cross traffic spots the nose first. [A17]
Why it matters: group_hint enter-vs-wait; prereq_hint sec04-F07; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F07.
Source: [A17 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A18
Painted crosswalks and invisible sidewalk extensions share one rule: raised hands or entering limbs and aids all claim the right of way. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint crosswalk-kinds; prereq_hint sec04-F15; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F15, sec04-F16.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A18
Ordinary walkers win crossings on intent, while cane and guide dog users win absolute held stops that outlast even green lights. [A18]
Why it matters: group_hint cane-priority; prereq_hint sec04-F17; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F15, sec04-F17.
Source: [A18 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0018]
FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A19
Bike passes need three feet of air with slow care, and skipping a bike yield costs doubled fines unlike ordinary yield slips. [A19]
Why it matters: group_hint bike-margins; prereq_hint sec04-F20; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F20, sec04-F21.
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A19
Slow bikes may be passed inside no passing zones when sight allows, yet bike lanes themselves forbid driving, parking and stopping except crossings and emergencies. [A19]
Why it matters: group_hint lane-vs-zone; prereq_hint sec04-F21; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec04-F20, sec04-F21.
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0019]
FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A20
Cars must never split a lane with a motorcycle, though two motorcycles themselves may legally share one lane side by side. [A20]
Why it matters: group_hint lane-share; prereq_hint sec04-F22; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F22, sec04-F23.
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0020]
FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A21
Front No-Zones punish early cut ins before whole fronts show in mirrors, while rear No-Zones punish tailgating that blinds both drivers forward. [A21]
Why it matters: group_hint nozone-ends; prereq_hint sec04-F28; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec04-F28, sec04-F29, sec04-F31.
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0021]
